title: Choose the CRM's shape
question: Safer register: no roll, you pick. Three conventional shapes plus the category standard, all light, minimal and roomy, held to a Notion and Attio craft bar.

options.label: The Quiet Table
options.thesis: The list is the product: one calm table you read across without a legend.
options.viewport: The lead table fills the screen, one hairline per row, rows tall enough to breathe, every column readable without a key.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of invisible, and without real density discipline it is just a spreadsheet.
options.case: Closest to Attio. Best if your instinct is to scan everything at once and act from the list.

options.label: The Reading Pane
options.thesis: Leads on the left, the open one in the middle, its history and next action on the right.
options.viewport: Three columns that never make you lose your place: pick a lead, read it, act on it, move to the next without a page change.
options.risk: Three columns get tight on a laptop and have to collapse carefully on a phone.
options.case: The fastest shape for working a queue, and the most natural fit for triaging Meta leads the moment they land.

options.label: The Notebook Shell
options.thesis: Almost no chrome: each view opens like a page, sections breathing under quiet headings.
options.viewport: A soft shell where today's work opens as a document, generous space between sections, controls appearing only where you are.
options.risk: Roomy shells hide density. A hundred overdue leads should not need scrolling through prose to find.
options.case: Closest to Notion. Best if calm and uncluttered matters more to you than seeing everything at once.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The arrangement every CRM ships, built to the craft level of Notion and Attio rather than to the average.
canonCard.viewport: Left icon rail, white ground, a pipeline board and a table view, one muted accent that only ever means something.
canonCard.risk: Recognisable from a mile away, which is the whole point and also the whole cost.
canonCard.case: No learning curve, nothing to explain, and nothing about it that is yours.
